verdicts.strongest_argument: This claim is weaker than 'priced' - it is unsupported, and its own admissible bars point the other way. The hunter records `body_available: false`: it never read the 13D/A. So the entire content of the finding is a cadence count over three accession numbers, with no knowledge of whether accession 0001734916-26-000004 reports an increased stake, a reduced stake, a financing, or boilerplate. The stated sign rests on the assertion that 'an exiting 5% holder typically files one final amendment and stops', which is not how Rule 13d-2 works - a holder selling down must amend promptly on each material change, so a string of three amendments (2025-12-12, 2026-06-30, 2026-08-11) is at least as consistent with a distribution as with an escalation. On publication: a Schedule 13D/A is a mandated public disclosure, indexed in the capture's own filings.json with an exact acceptance instant, and it is the kind of filing professional ownership screens flag the same evening; the corpus's silence is a statement about the capture's query set (100 of 103 items are EDGAR index rows, no news documents at all), not about what filing-screen subscribers saw. Then the admissible tape: the amendment was accepted 2026-08-11T21:21:42Z after the close, and 2026-08-12 closed 20.63 against 21.20, -2.7%, on 334,300 shares - below the 447k average - followed by a steady grind to 19.36 by 2026-09-01. There is no activist bid visible anywhere in the window; the only above-average volume day is 08-24 (880,000 shares) on a -2.6% close. A finding signed positive on 'live campaign' has to explain why the market marked the stock down on low volume in the eleven sessions after the filing became public. Finally the mechanism does not reach this print: a 13D amendment does not change what Daktronics reports for its fiscal Q1 on 2026-09-02, and the baseline's 14.86% median reaction is driven by results, not by an ownership filing three weeks stale by the time the numbers land.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The Schedule 13D/A itself is a public EDGAR filing with a timestamped acceptance instant - a mandated disclosure, not a private datum.

A public risk-factor diff dated 2026-06-25 already names 'leadership transition risk, and activist-driven strategic shifts' as newly added 10-K risk factors, so the existence of an activist overhang was in circulation ten weeks before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Admissible bars only (clean-view excludes the 2026-09-02 bar and the 20260902T150741Z snapshot; for a bmo print the 09-02 close is the reaction). 08-11 close 21.20 -> 08-12 20.63 (-2.7%) on 334,300 shares, below the 447k 20d average, then a monotone drift to 19.36 on 09-01, -10.08% over twenty sessions. The one high-volume session (08-24, 880,000 shares) closed down 2.6%. Nothing in the admissible window looks like an accumulating holder, which is the opposite of the finding's sign.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Reading the actual 13D/A body and finding it reports an increased position, a nominating notice or a strategic-alternatives demand - and a volume signature in the admissible bars consistent with accumulation rather than the low-volume markdown the tape actually shows.

interactions: The main claim and its 'independence' support both terminate in the same filings.json index; the only non-EDGAR corroboration (the d-risk 10-K diff) is a June document about risk-factor language, not about the August amendment, so it does not independently date or size the campaign.
corpus_limits: Per clean-view/DAKT.json I excluded snapshot 20260902T150741Z and the 2026-09-02 bar entirely, so I could not see any 09-01/09-02 news sweep or the event-day tape. The capture holds no body for the 13D/A, so neither the hunter nor I could read what the amendment actually says - the decisive fact is absent from the corpus. DAKT's capture has no news items, so the absence of coverage of the amendment is a capture artefact and I have not scored it as non-publication.
